message: Firewall {family} {id} chain's default action is "accept" - traffic not matched by any rule is allowed through.
description: VyOS's own documented behavior: an unset default-action on a base chain defaults to accept, exactly as permissive as an explicit one, not a safer 'no policy yet' state (docs.vyos.io/.../firewall/ipv4.html). Custom chains and the output base chain (traffic the router itself originates, not traffic reaching it) are deliberately excluded - output defaulting to accept is the normal, expected case for nearly every router.

message: SSH password authentication is enabled - consider key-only login (service ssh disable-password-authentication).
description: Flags SSH password authentication being allowed (VyOS's own disable-password-authentication flag not set) while SSH is actually enabled. Wrapped in [ssh][...] (a one-element multiselect list) since `ssh` in the facts object is a single object, not an array - every rule's query must return an array so the same one-match-per-array-element evaluation model applies uniformly.

message: The HTTPS API has no client address restriction configured (service https allow-client address).
description: Flags the HTTPS API being enabled with no client address restriction at all - any host that can reach the API port can attempt to authenticate against it.

message: SNMP community "{name}" is a well-known default string.
description: Flags any SNMP v1/v2c community using a well-known default string, checked case-insensitively via the precomputed `nameLower` field (JMESPath has no built-in lower-case function - see buildConfigWarningFacts). A community's name is the tagNode identifier itself, not a masked leaf value, so it's fully readable here.

message: User "{username}" has no password and no SSH key configured.
description: Flags any enabled local user account with no authentication factor configured at all - no password hash and no SSH public key with actual key data. This is the checkable subset of 'empty secrets': every secret this app models is write-only (values never sent back), so 'no secret configured for an account that isn't disabled' is the only checkable form.
